models.model_label: Mandatory IFRS adoption and cost of equity (full-period pooled regression, Table 4 Panel A)
models.sample_description: The full-sample pooled firm-year regression covers 6,456 observations from 18 EU countries during 1995–2006, representing 1,084 distinct firms. Firms must have data in both the pre- and post-mandatory periods and the data needed for the specified controls; the main sample excludes firms in the three stated classes exempted from 2005 mandatory adoption. Compustat Global provides financial-statement and adoption data; I/B/E/S provides the stock prices and analyst forecasts used to construct COC. Price and forecast inputs are taken seven months after fiscal year-end. The estimation sample requires current stock-price data, positive analyst mean consensus earnings forecasts for at least two periods ahead, all four implied cost-of-equity measures, and available controls; cost-of-equity estimates below 0 or above 1 are omitted.
models.method_details: Table 4 Panel A labels the fit “Pooled Regressions.” The reviewed equation, design description, and table notes do not identify the underlying estimator, so it remains unknown.

dependent_variable.name: COC
dependent_variable.definition: Mean of four implied cost-of-equity estimates: Claus and Thomas (2001), Gebhardt et al. (2001), Gode and Mohanram (2003), and Easton (2004). The estimates are based on current stock prices and analysts’ forecasts; the price and forecast inputs are measured seven months after fiscal year-end.
dependent_variable.formula: Arithmetic mean of the four implied cost-of-equity estimates

evidence.quote: COC       - the mean of the four implied cost of equity estimates based

I use a measure that relies on four estimation models: the industry ROE model in Gebhardt et al. (2001), the economywide growth model in Claus and Thomas (2001), the unrestricted abnormal earnings growth model in Gode and Mohanram (2003), and the restricted abnormal earnings growth model in Easton (2004).

These price and forecast data are in local currencies and are taken seven months after the fiscal year-end to ensure the financial data are publicly available and priced at the time of estimation (Hail and Leuz 2006).

models.equation_text: COC = α0 + α1 MandatoryIFRSAdopter + α2 PostAdoption + α3(MandatoryIFRSAdopter × PostAdoption) + α4 PP + α5 OTC + α6 EXCH + α7 INFLA + α8 SIZE + α9 RETVAR + α10 LEV + αm DIndustry + αn DCountry + ε

fixed_effects.details: Separate industry and country indicator-variable fixed-effect dimensions. Industry indicators follow Campbell (1996); country indicators identify countries. The equation/table do not list year fixed effects; year appears in the two-way clustering.

evidence.quote: indicator variables to control for industry and country fixed effects
Industry controls Included
Country controls Included
Industry controls                 - indicator variables indicating a firm’s industry membership based on the industry classification in Campbell
Country controls                - indicator variables for countries.

standard_errors.details: Two-way cluster-adjusted t-statistics by firm and year; p-values are two-tailed.

evidence.quote: Panel A reports the coefficients, firm and year cluster-adjusted t-statistics, and two-tailed p-values of the regression model for the full sample period (1995 to 2006)
Panel A reports the pooled regression coefficients, firm, and year cluster-adjusted t-statistics, and two-tailed p-values
Intercept 0.0841

estimation_procedure.description: Difference-in-differences design: compare the change in COC between the pre-mandatory period (1995–2004) and post-mandatory period (2005–2006) for mandatory adopters with the corresponding change for voluntary adopters. The fitted baseline is one pooled regression over the full 1995–2006 sample; the interaction between mandatory-adopter and post-period indicators is the central treatment contrast. The 2004/2005-excluded regression is a sensitivity fit; Table 4 Panels B and C reconstruct 2×2 comparisons from Panel A coefficients rather than reporting separate fits.

evidence.quote: This difference-in-differences design, which analyzes the population of both mandatory and voluntary adopters over the full period from 1995 to 2006, compares the change in the cost of equity for mandatory adopters before and after the mandatory switch relative to the corresponding change in the cost of equity for voluntary adopters.
Therefore, for ease of exposition, Panel B reports the reconstructed coefficients and the significance levels in a 2 - 2 analysis for the full sample period.
Panel B reports the 2 - 2 analysis of mandatory adopters versus voluntary adopters by period for the full sample, constructed using the coefficients in Panel A.

preprocessing.description: The COC inputs are based on current stock price data and analyst mean consensus earnings forecasts for at least two periods ahead. Prices and forecasts are taken seven months after fiscal year-end; forecasts must be positive; long-term EPS growth forecasts are used when three- through five-year-ahead forecasts are missing.

evidence.quote: These price and forecast data are in local currencies and are taken seven months after the fiscal year-end to ensure the financial data are publicly available and priced at the time of estimation (Hail and Leuz 2006).
To be included in the sample, I require each firm-year observation to have current stock price data and analyst mean consensus earnings forecasts for at least two periods ahead.
All earnings forecasts are restricted to be positive, and the long-term earnings growth rate forecasts are used if the three-year- through five-year-ahead earnings forecasts are missing.

preprocessing.description: The dividend payout ratio is the historic three-year firm average, replaced by the country-year median if missing or outside 0–1. All four individual implied cost-of-equity measures are required to compute COC; estimates below 0 or above 1 are omitted.

evidence.quote: The dividend payout ratio is computed using the historic three-year average for each firm,
and is replaced by the country-year median payout ratio when missing or out of the range of 0 to 1 (Hail and Leuz 2006).
I further require that all four individual measures of cost of equity be available in order to calculate the average cost of equity measure.
Cost of equity estimates below 0 and above 1 are omitted.

scope.quote: This study examines whether the mandatory adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) in the European Union (EU) in 2005 reduces the cost of equity capital.
This difference-in-differences design, which analyzes the population of both mandatory and voluntary adopters over the full period from 1995 to 2006

equation.quote: COC = alpha_0 + alpha_1*MandatoryIFRSAdopter + alpha_2*PostAdoption + alpha_3*(MandatoryIFRSAdopter*PostAdoption) + alpha_4*PP + alpha_5*OTC + alpha_6*EXCH + alpha_7*INFLA + alpha_8*SIZE + alpha_9*RETVAR + alpha_10*LEV + alpha_m*DIndustry + alpha_n*DCountry + epsilon.

sample.quote: the full period sample of 6,456 firm-year observations from 1995 to 2006

dependencies.quote: I use a measure that relies on four estimation models: the industry ROE model in Gebhardt et al. review_notes: Source-first scope selection: Table 4 Panel A, full period 1995–2006, Equation (1) is the principal full-sample test of the mandatory IFRS effect on COC. The full-sample DID specification retains the author’s complete control set and central mandatory-adopter × post-period interaction.

Excluded the transition-period specification as sensitivity analysis, Table 4 Panels B/C as algebraically reconstructed two-by-two comparisons rather than separate fits, and Table 6 legal-enforcement/disclosure/comparability conditioning analyses as follow-up heterogeneity/mechanism tests. Later bid-ask, sample restriction, and self-selection analyses are sensitivity checks. These exclusions follow the one-principal-family scope rule.

COC is the average of four established implied-cost-of-equity valuation estimates. The paper identifies those inputs and their required price/forecast data and screening, but reports no separate fitted regression needed to generate them; they are outcome measurement inputs, so dependencies remain empty.
Underlying estimator remains unknown: “pooled regressions” and firm/year cluster-adjusted t-statistics do not establish OLS or another estimator.
